content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a full trace of each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement back to the disclosure.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. I checked all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and dependent claims 2-12, 14-17, 19-22) limitation by limitation, all 27 entries of the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part as used in the Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all seven figure briefs (FIG. 1-7) together with the Brief Description of the Drawings, against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is a truncated copy of the disclosure and adds nothing). input/brief.md was used only for formalities (title, applicant/inventor, no priority claim, no federal sponsorship, apparatus plus method claims, no means-plus-function, preserved terminology). Result on disclosure fidelity: no untraced technical assertion was found. Every structural element (rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot through the rail, printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, with a downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge, releasably held by two screws in two corresponding holes and reversible from one longitudinal side to the opposite side so the same marked upper face serves either edge; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing hole separation; two separate guide carriages on the upper face, each with a lower key in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding, one cylindrical drill bushing whose vertical bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with the slot, the two bore axes parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face, a threaded clamp knob above the rail whose shank passes through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail so tightening clamps the rail between carriage and shoe and loosening frees it, and its own pointer aligned with its bore axis and read against the distance marks so the difference of readings is the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the rail midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the center index; rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers and knobs; hardened-metal replaceable bushings; no motor, battery, electronic sensor or network connection; and the full setting, placing, aligning, drilling and lifting-away method) traces to an exact affirmative passage. Background prior-art characterizations were left unchallenged as permitted. Figure briefs contain no unsupported functional-surface geometry: the schematic blocks, round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence, graduation-line marks and ragged break line are shape-neutral depiction conventions for parts the inventor affirmatively disclosed, no depth, taper, angle, runout or undisclosed contact topology is verbalized, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaked into the application text. Section-line designations are consistent across FIG-2 (lines 3-3 and 5-5), the Brief Description, FIG-3, FIG-5 and the Detailed Description; each numeral means exactly one part; no placeholder, drafting note, open question or unresolved alternative remains. Two verified internal inconsistencies are reported: claim 19 requires the projecting portion to press directly on the straight edge while simultaneously interposing the spacer plate, contradicting the Detailed Description; and the Detailed Description, claim 6 and the FIG-7 brief assert that one straight centerline is simultaneously coincident with a transverse center index at the rail midpoint and with a sight notch at the second end that the same sentence says are spaced apart along the rail, which is geometrically impossible and leaves the renderer without a determinate centerline direction. Both fixes are removal-only or source-word substitutions and add no new matter.

findings.title: Claim 19 requires the fence portion to bear on the straight edge and on the interposed spacer plate at the same time
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 19 (with claim 18, seventh step); draft/08-detailed-description.md, method paragraph
findings.detail: Claim 18 recites "placing the flat lower face on the front face of the workpiece and pressing the downwardly projecting portion of the fence against the straight edge". Claim 19 adds "before pressing the downwardly projecting portion against the straight edge, fitting a spacer plate having parallel opposite faces between the downwardly projecting portion and the straight edge". Once the plate is between them, the projecting portion cannot press against the straight edge; it presses against the near face of the plate while the far face bears on the edge. The Detailed Description states the correct relationship, so the claim and the description do not use the same relationship for the same step.
findings.evidence: Claim 19: "further comprising, before pressing the downwardly projecting portion against the straight edge, fitting a spacer plate having parallel opposite faces between the downwardly projecting portion and the straight edge". Detailed Description: "The downwardly projecting portion 32 of the fence 30, or the outer face of the spacer plate 40 when the spacer plate 40 is fitted, is pressed against the selected workpiece edge 92, which fixes the setback." Disclosure: "A removable spacer plate can be fitted between the fence and the workpiece edge."
findings.fix: Replace claim 19 with: "19. The method of claim 18, wherein pressing the downwardly projecting portion of the fence against the straight edge comprises first fitting a spacer plate having parallel opposite faces between the downwardly projecting portion and the straight edge and then pressing the downwardly projecting portion against one of the parallel opposite faces of the spacer plate while the other of the parallel opposite faces bears against the straight edge, whereby a setback of both holes of the pair from the straight edge is increased by a thickness of the spacer plate and a separation between the holes of the pair is unchanged."

findings.title: One straight centerline is required to coincide with both the transverse center index at the rail midpoint and the sight notch at the second end, which the same sentence says are spaced apart along the rail
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 7 paragraph; draft/09-claims.md, claim 6; figures/FIG-7.md, centerline paragraph
findings.detail: The draft states that the transverse center index 24 "runs across the rail 10 transverse to the length of the rail 10" at the midpoint, that the sight notch 26 is formed in the second end, that the two features "are spaced apart along the rail 10", and that sighting them together "brings both of those features onto the centerline 94". A single straight line cannot be coincident with a mark running transverse to the rail at the midpoint and also with a notch at the far end when the two are spaced apart lengthwise. Claim 6 recites the same impossible pair of relationships, and the FIG-7 brief instructs the renderer to draw "a single straight line" aligned with both, without specifying its direction, so the drawing cannot be made consistent with the text. The sentence asserting simultaneous coincidence and the "spaced apart" characterization are additions; the disclosure says only that the user "can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline", and never says both lie on that line at once or that they are spaced apart along the rail.
findings.evidence: Detailed Description: "Sighting the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 together on the centerline 94 brings both of those features onto the centerline 94, and the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10." Claim 6: "wherein the sight notch and the transverse center index are spaced apart along the rail and are alignable together with a centerline marked on the front face of the workpiece." FIG-7 brief: "A centerline 94 is a single straight line drawn on the workpiece 90 and is aligned with the transverse center index 24 and with the sight notch 26." Nearest source passage: "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint. A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index. The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs."
findings.fix: (a) In draft/08-detailed-description.md, delete the sentence "Sighting the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 together on the centerline 94 brings both of those features onto the centerline 94, and the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10." and replace it with: "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 are aligned with one another, and the user aligns the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 with the centerline 94 before drilling." (b) In claim 6, delete "the sight notch and the transverse center index are spaced apart along the rail and", so the claim reads: "6. The drilling jig of claim 5, wherein the sight notch and the transverse center index are alignable together with a centerline marked on the front face of the workpiece." (c) In figures/FIG-7.md, replace the centerline paragraph with: "A centerline 94 is a single straight line drawn on the workpiece 90, running across the band transverse to the length of the rail 10 and coincident with the transverse center index 24, and visible on the workpiece 90 on both sides of the band."
